Definition: to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
BiblicalUsage: Cain cries that his punishment is greater than he can bear, and Moses offers himself in place of the people, asking to be blotted out of God's book rather than see them destroyed. The scapegoat carries the iniquities of Israel away into the wilderness, and the Servant of the LORD takes up our griefs and carries our sorrows as His own.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the word that holds the gospel together: what I cannot carry, another carries for me. The guilt is lifted off my shoulders and laid on the One who bears it away, and that is why I can stand forgiven.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
